hooks.text: Chicago blamed a cow for a fire with no proven cause.

title: Chicago's Cow Was Cleared 126 Years After the Fire
description: The cause of the 1871 Great Chicago Fire remains unknown. Catherine O'Leary was exonerated in 1997, and the famous cow story has a disputed history.

beats.text: Chicago blamed a cow for a fire with no proven cause.
beats.visual: Period illustration of the Mrs. O’Leary cow legend, presented as folklore.
queries: Mrs O Leary cow Chicago Fire illustration

beats.text: In 1871, flames began near Catherine O’Leary’s barn.
beats.visual: 1871 Currier and Ives lithograph of Chicago in flames.

beats.text: The fire left a hundred thousand people homeless.
beats.visual: 1871 stereograph of the ruined Cook County Courthouse.

beats.text: O’Leary swore she was asleep when it began.
beats.visual: Period caricature of the O’Leary legend, used as symbolic art rather than a portrait.
queries: Mrs O Leary cow period caricature

beats.text: The official inquiry found no proof against her.
beats.visual: Designed fact card quoting the inquiry’s conclusion.

beats.text: Years later, Michael Ahern boasted that he and others invented the cow story.
beats.visual: Return to the cow illustration while narration attributes Ahern’s disputed boast.

better_than_last: The inquiry and Ahern’s disputed later boast are now distinct claims; the fire cause stays unknown.
